deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft for the Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen (1857). It is written on a printed ledger form with columns for Auslage, Porto and Franko. The page has four parts.

(A) Top lines, mostly struck through and only partly legible. They continue the previous page on the Dirichlet/minimum principle. Functions on the surface are to have prescribed arbitrary discontinuities, and the Dirichlet-type integral
  ∫((∂α/∂x − ∂β/∂y)^2 + (∂α/∂y + ∂β/∂x)^2) dS
must stay finite. Through the 'Minimumsmethode' this yields the existence of functions with given singularities. Below this stands an unrelated name ('Eduard ... aus Ansbach'), probably ledger or personal matter.

(B) Local behaviour at a branch point. Let z be a function on the Riemann surface and ζ another variable. Near a point with z = z', ζ = ζ' where μ+1 sheets of z hang together, ζ − ζ' is a local parameter (small of first order). Then
  (z − z')/(ζ − ζ')^{μ+1}
and
  (∂z/∂ζ)/(ζ − ζ')^μ
stay finite and nonzero. So ∂z/∂ζ vanishes to order μ there. At z = ∞ the variable 1/z is used instead.

So ∂z/∂ζ is zero or infinite only at finitely many points. By the argument principle, ∫ d log(∂z/∂ζ) taken around the boundary of the cut surface T' equals the sum of integrals around those points, i.e. 2πi·(zeros − poles). Riemann gets w·2πi − 2n·2πi:
- w = Σμ is the total branching number of the n-sheeted surface over the z-plane.
- At each of the n points over z = ∞, with z = 1/t, dz/dt = −1/t^2 has a double pole. This gives 2n. (Making this explicit is mine.)

The integral is then computed a second way, via the decomposition
  log ∂z/∂ζ = log ∂z/∂s + log ∂s/∂σ − log ∂ζ/∂σ
with auxiliary variables s, σ. The intermediate values are only partly written ('(2p−1)', the second left blank). The conclusion is
  ∫ d log(∂z/∂ζ) = (2p − 2)·2πi, hence w − 2n = 2p − 2,
i.e. p = w/2 − n + 1. This is Riemann's genus formula for an n-sheeted branched cover of the sphere, as in §7 of the 1857 paper. The second count rests on the boundary of T' (2p cross-cuts), whose total contribution to d log of a ratio of differentials is (2p−2)·2πi. That is equivalent to deg K = 2p − 2.

(C) Middle, partly struck. 'Bestimmung der Anzahl der ...': the number of branch points is to be determined from the equation F(ζ, z) = 0. The sentence on a general algebraic function of s, z (the s',z' / Verzweigungsart wording) continues as follows. A function that becomes infinite of first order at m' arbitrarily given points (s, z) contains m' − p + 1 arbitrary constants, entering linearly (the Riemann inequality / Riemann part of Riemann–Roch for general position). It is announced that such functions can be expressed rationally in s and z, with F(s, z) = 0 of degree n in s and m in z.

(D) Bottom, heavily struck. Degree bounds ν ≥ n − 1, μ ≥ m − 1 for the numerator polynomial in s, z. There is a product X(ζ)X(ζ1)...X(ζν) and a phrase on a polynomial 'of degree (m+n)', presumably in s, z or ζ. The aim is to construct the function s' as a quotient of polynomials vanishing at prescribed points, i.e. the adjoint-polynomial representation of §§9–10 of the 1857 paper. The text breaks off: 'Die Function s' wird ...'.
errors: The intermediate value '∫ d log(∂z/∂s) = (2p−1)' (without 2πi) does not fit the final (2p−2)·2πi as written. It looks like an unfinished draft line, with the companion integral ∫ d log(∂ζ/∂σ) left blank. The final result w − 2n = 2p − 2 is correct.
The argument assumes simple general position (no branching over z = ∞, ζ − ζ' a local parameter). This is implicit but standard.

results.what: Order of vanishing of dz/dζ at a branch point of multiplicity μ+1: (z−z')/(ζ−ζ')^{μ+1} and (dz/dζ)/(ζ−ζ')^μ finite
results.modern_name: local normal form of a branched covering / ramification index

results.what: Counting zeros minus poles of dz/dζ via ∫ d log; w − 2n = 2p − 2
results.modern_name: Riemann–Hurwitz formula for a degree-n cover of P^1 (genus formula p = w/2 − n + 1)

results.what: Existence of functions with prescribed singularities via the minimum (Dirichlet) principle
Functions with m' simple poles at given points depend linearly on m' − p + 1 constants and are rational in s, z
results.modern_name: Riemann inequality (Riemann part of Riemann–Roch); representation by adjoint polynomials
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857; Roch 1865 for the correction term

deep.surprise_reason: Everything on the page is draft material for results Riemann published in 1857: the Dirichlet principle, w − 2n = 2p − 2, and m − p + 1 constants with rational representation. The only minor interest is the variant d log(dz/dζ) route to the genus formula through intermediate variables.

checkable.sympy: z = zeta**(mu+1); simplify(diff(z,zeta)/zeta**mu) == mu+1  (with mu a positive integer symbol)
checkable.asserts: At a branch point of order μ+1, dz/dζ vanishes to order μ with nonzero finite quotient
At z = ∞ with local parameter t = 1/z, dz/dt has a double pole, giving 2 per sheet (total 2n)
Hyperelliptic check: a 2-sheeted cover with 2p+2 branch points satisfies w − 2n = 2p − 2
Placeholder consistency check of the genus formula p = w/2 − n + 1 against a curve with known branching (adapt w, n to a concrete smooth model)

transcription_corrections: 'Edward Tallinge aus Ansbach' is more plausibly 'Eduard ... aus Ansbach' (a personal name, unrelated to the mathematics).
In the local formula the image reads (z−z')/(ζ−ζ')^{μ+1} = ∂z/(∂ζ (ζ−ζ')^μ) up to a constant factor, i.e. a statement of finiteness rather than an exact equality.
'diese ist also = w 2πi − 2n·2πi' is confirmed; the later 'folglich w − 2n = 2p − 2' is clearly legible.
'∫ d log ∂z/∂s = (2p−1)' is uncertain; the image shows a struck/unfinished line, possibly '(2p−2)' or incomplete.
